title: Psychological Wellbeing (18 items)
summary: A short check of six areas of wellbeing: autonomy, mastery, growth, relationships, purpose and self-acceptance.
clinicianNotes: Published 18-item Ryff Psychological Wellbeing measure (3 items per area, 7-point agree scale). Items 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 17 and 18 are reverse scored, as in the supplied scoring sheet. Each area is a sum of 3 items (3 to 21); higher means higher wellbeing. The sheet gives no cut-offs or norms, so results are shown as bars without bands. The sheet gives no licence line: the reviewing psychologist should confirm the wording may be used before this pack is marked reviewed.
prompt: Please choose how much you agree or disagree with each statement.

source.attribution: Psychological Wellbeing 18-item version (Ryff & Keyes, 1995), as listed in the SPARQtools.org Measuring Mobility toolkit; MIDUS II documentation (Ryff et al., 2010).

subscales.label: Autonomy
subscales.description: Independence of thought and standing by your own views.

subscales.label: Environmental mastery
subscales.description: Feeling able to manage daily life and surroundings.

subscales.label: Personal growth
subscales.description: Feeling open to learning and continuing to develop.

subscales.label: Purpose in life
subscales.description: Having goals and a sense that life has direction.

subscales.label: Self-acceptance
subscales.description: A positive attitude toward yourself and your past.

items.text: I like most parts of my personality.
When I look at the story of my life, I am pleased with how things have turned out so far.
Some people wander aimlessly through life, but I am not one of them.
The demands of everyday life often get me down.
In many ways I feel disappointed about my achievements in life.
Maintaining close relationships has been difficult and frustrating for me.
I live life one day at a time and don't really think about the future.
In general, I feel I am in charge of the situation in which I live.
I am good at managing the responsibilities of daily life.
I sometimes feel as if I've done all there is to do in life.
For me, life has been a continuous process of learning, changing, and growth.
I think it is important to have new experiences that challenge how I think about myself and the world.
People would describe me as a giving person, willing to share my time with others.
I gave up trying to make big improvements or changes in my life a long time ago.
I tend to be influenced by people with strong opinions.
I have not experienced many warm and trusting relationships with others.
I have confidence in my own opinions, even if they are different from the way most other people think.
I judge myself by what I think is important, not by the values of what others think is important.
